newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Caymans stock exchange chief appointed.
newsitem.headline: Caymans stock exchange chief appointed.

text.p: Ann Nealon, a former official with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, has been appointed chief executive officer of the new Cayman Islands Stock Exchange, the government announced Friday.
Nealon replaces David Carrad, who was on loan from International Securities Consultants of Hong Kong, as head of the newly formed exchange.
Officially formed on January 1, the exchange has yet to make its first listing.
Nealon, a lawyer originally from London, is the former director of policy for the Hong Kong exchange.
The Stock Exchange Authority, which governs operations of the exchange, is accepting and approving listings of international mutual funds, which will be the first items traded on the exchange.
Eurobonds, Class A stocks of worldwide companies, and other instruments of trading will come later, according to Authority Chairman Anthony Travers.
The CSX has completed and approved an initial list of agents who will be authorized to trade on the exchange. The agents currently are submitting their lists of funds to be approved for trade.
The exchange was to have been operational this month. No date for the official start of trading has been announced.
The Cayman Islands, a British territory in the western Caribbean, are known as an offshore financial center and upscale tourist destination.
The islands, with a population of 35,000, have 560 registered financial institutions with assets of $460 billion.
